cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

The Business Services Analyst provides professional financial and business services support to the UCPD Business Services Unit and helps ensure departmental financial transactions are accurate, timely, compliant, and properly documented. The position supports day-to-day financial operations across purchasing, accounts payable and receivable, reimbursements, travel, recharge billing, deposits, reconciliations, MOU and contract administration, financial monitoring, and customer service.
Purchasing, Accounts Payable, and BluCard Transactions - 30%

The position independently researches and resolves financial and transactional issues of moderate scope and complexity within established University policies and procedures, maintains accurate and audit-ready financial records, and identifies issues requiring correction or escalation. By providing consistent transaction processing, reconciliation, monitoring, and customer support, the position helps maintain effective internal controls and supports the efficient financial administration of UCPD operations.

Reviews and processes purchasing, accounts payable, BluCard, and vendor-payment requests of moderate scope and complexity. Creates BearBuy requisitions; verifies chartstrings, business purpose, approvals, receipts, receiving records, and supporting documentation; researches documentation, vendor, payment, and policy issues; and determines appropriate action within established guidelines. Serves as a primary processor for the BSU shared inbox on assigned days and supports departmental cardholders. Escalates covered services, purchases with an anticipated total value of $100,000 or more, policy exceptions, and material concerns to the Business Services Manager.

As part of a public safety department, the position may be required, at the discretion of department management and based on operational needs, to work occasional overtime or outside of regularly scheduled hours, including evenings and weekends. Such assignments may include support for home football games, demonstrations, major campus events, emergencies, or other significant departmental activities.
Reimbursements, Travel, Direct Bills, and Employee Payments - 15%

Reviews and processes travel, entertainment, relocation, direct-bill, registration, and other reimbursement or employee-payment requests. Applies University policies, verifies allowability and approvals, researches eligibility and documentation issues, coordinates routine corrections, and maintains complete supporting records.
Accounts Receivable, Event and False-Alarm Recharges, and Deposits - 15%

Reviews event records, approved rates, chartstrings, dispatch data, and supporting documentation to prepare event invoices, recharge journals, false-alarm billing, and deposits. Reconciles billing and deposit information, researches discrepancies, obtains missing information, and maintains complete audit-ready records.
Financial Monitoring, Reconciliation, and Reporting - 15%

Performs assigned vendor, fleet charge, card-program, ledger, and limited-activity fund reconciliations. Researches unexpected activity, missing documentation, delayed transactions, and posting discrepancies; prepares summaries of findings and recommended corrective actions; and identifies potential compliance or internal-control concerns for escalation to the Business Services Manager when appropriate.
MOU, Recharge, Contract, and Campus Support - 15%

Supports administration of departmental MOUs and recharge services. Maintains documentation and signature trackers, obtains chartstrings and supporting information, follows up on outstanding items, assists with monthly billing and payment tracking, monitors deadlines and deliverables, and prepares status information for the Business Services Manager. Collaborates with the FSA3 as a departmental subject-matter resource when appropriate.
Customer Service, Audit Support, Procedures, and Process Improvement - 10%

Serves as a resource to departmental staff, campus partners, and vendors regarding established financial procedures, documentation requirements, and transaction status. Maintains desk manuals and workflow documentation, supports audits and financial reviews, evaluates recurring problems, and recommends improvements to accuracy, timeliness, customer service, and internal controls.
Proficiency in spreadsheet and database software used for financial analysis, reconciliation, tracking, and reporting.
Must maintain valid CA DL and clean DMV record.
Working knowledge of financial processes, policies and procedures.
Working knowledge of University financial systems and purchasing, travel, reimbursement, recharge, or cashiering practices.
Strong knowledge of financial data management and reporting systems.
Skills to provide procedural guidance or coaching to staff regarding established financial processes and requirements.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to review information from multiple sources, identify discrepancies, evaluate relevant factors, and determine appropriate action within established guidelines.

Strong interpersonal, customer service, verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain financial procedures and documentation requirements clearly to departmental staff, campus partners, and vendors.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a high-volume environment.
Sound judgment and decision-making skills, including the ability to recognize matters requiring escalation to the Business Services Manager.
Ability to function effectively as a member of a team and adapt to changing priorities.
Intermediate knowledge and understanding of internal-control practices and their impact on protecting University resources.
